Anchor.description: A path, and optionally a symbol, in the repository, optionally pinned to a commit.

CommitId.description: A git object id: 40 lowercase hex digits (SHA-1) or 64 (SHA-256).

AnchorCitation.description: A code location the claim rests on.

MessageCitation.description: A message in the conversation, by the identifier the driver gave it.

Ref.description:
An identifier the driver gave the model: a message, a tool call, an earlier
MFP message or a decision. A model never invents one.

ToolResultCitation.description: The result of a tool call, by the call's identifier.

RecordCitation.description: An earlier MFP message, by the identifier its receiver gave it.

Citations.description: A citation list that must not be empty.

Shape.description:
A structural type, the value of a `shape` proposition. Objects list their
fields; `opaque` names a type the writer could not see into.

optional.description: Whether the field may be absent.

strength.description:
The holder's kind of reliance, not a confidence. `must`: the holder breaks
if the proposition is false. `should`: it degrades. Comparison never reads it.

SubjectKey.description:
A named concept in the codebase, as dot-separated segments of lowercase
letters, digits and inner hyphens, e.g. `authz.permission-evaluation`. Keys
are hierarchical: `authz` is an ancestor of `authz.permission-evaluation`.

Scope.description:
Where a proposition holds, as `;`-separated `dimension:atom|atom` parts, e.g.
`env:prod|staging;tenant:t1`. A dimension appears at most once. Absent means
everywhere.

FreshnessValue.description:
How stale a reader of the subject can be, from least to most:
`per-call`, `per-request`, `per-session`, `ttl:<seconds>` and `static`.

strength.description:
The holder's kind of reliance, not a confidence. `must`: the holder breaks
if the proposition is false. `should`: it degrades. Comparison never reads it.

ConsistencyValue.description:
How strong a reader's view of the subject is, from weakest to strongest:
`eventual`, `bounded:<seconds>` (a smaller bound is stronger),
`read-your-writes` and `linearizable`.

CardinalityValue.description: How many times something happens, from strongest guarantee to weakest.

InvariantPremise.description: Free text, compared only by a model.

Text.description: Text a reader is meant to read: at least one non-space character.

InvalidationEffect.description: Only an effect takes the invalidation form: a premise states the freshness it relies on.

InvalidationValue.description:
The effect form "cached at a freshness, evicted on these events":
`<freshness> invalidated-on <event>,<event>`, the events sorted, each once.

OrderingEffect.description: The subject is the first event of the pair and the value the second.

FootprintEntry.description: A path or symbol a change edits, creates or deletes.

profile.description: The profile the message conforms to, by URI. Absent means the core profile.

confidence.description: The model's own confidence in this report. An opinion about an opinion: it never carries weight.

goal.description: What the change will achieve, in one or two sentences.

footprint.description: The paths and symbols it expects to edit, create or delete.

premises.description: What it relies on, about code it does not own.

declaredEffects.description: Effects it expects to cause. A receiver derives effects; these are advisory.

Intent.description: What a model will do, and what it relies on, before it writes code.

PremiseProposition.description: What a model relies on about code it does not own.

EffectProposition.description: What a model expects a change to alter.

profile.description: The profile the message conforms to, by URI. Absent means the core profile.

confidence.description: The model's own confidence in this report. An opinion about an opinion: it never carries weight.

Premise.description: One more thing the model relies on, after its intent.

profile.description: The profile the message conforms to, by URI. Absent means the core profile.

confidence.description: The model's own confidence in this report. An opinion about an opinion: it never carries weight.

Decision.description: A choice the model made, why, and what it rejected.

profile.description: The profile the message conforms to, by URI. Absent means the core profile.

confidence.description: The model's own confidence in this report. An opinion about an opinion: it never carries weight.

category.description: What kind of thing was noticed. Open in the core; a profile may close it.

Observation.description: Something the model noticed, and what it rests on.

Token.description: A lowercase token: letters, digits and inner hyphens, e.g. `request-changes`.

profile.description: The profile the message conforms to, by URI. Absent means the core profile.

confidence.description: The model's own confidence in this report. An opinion about an opinion: it never carries weight.

decision.description: The decision, by the identifier the driver gave it.

argument.description: Why the decision applies, does not apply, or should be overruled.

Stance.description: How the model's work relates to an earlier decision it met as precedent.

profile.description: The profile the message conforms to, by URI. Absent means the core profile.

confidence.description: The model's own confidence in this report. An opinion about an opinion: it never carries weight.

outcome.description:
The outcome, as a token. The core profile's vocabulary is `accept`,
`revise`, `reject` and `defer`; a profile may replace it.

residualRisk.description: What could still go wrong if the outcome is taken.

Verdict.description: The outcome the model thinks a piece of work should have. An opinion, never a ruling.

kind.description: `<kind>`: the message kind the member belongs to.

schema.description: A JSON Schema for the member's value.

required.description: Whether a message of that kind must carry it.

ProfileMember.description: A message member a profile adds, under its own prefix.

id.description: The profile's URI. Messages name it in `profile`.

mfp.description: The MFP version the profile narrows.

prefix.description: The prefix its members are named under. Required when it defines members.

vocabularies.description: The open vocabularies it closes, each to a non-empty set of tokens.

require.description: Optional core members it requires, as `<kind>.<member>`, e.g. `intent.footprint`.

Profile.description:
A profile: a named narrowing of the core for one domain. It may close the
open vocabularies, require optional members, and add members under its
prefix. It can only narrow: every message valid under a profile is valid
under the core wire schema.

Prefix.description:
A reverse-DNS name a vendor controls, e.g. `org.example.review`. A
profile's members are named `<prefix>/<name>`.

Predicate.description: The dimension a proposition talks about. Each predicate orders its values; see lattices.md.

Relation.description: How a proposition's value sits on its predicate's order. Each predicate takes some of these.
